title: Funny Pet Dancing Expression Video
description: A detailed multi-stage video generation prompt for creating a realistic pet dancing video with exaggerated 3D facial expressions and rhythmic movements.
promptText:
[Style]
Funny live-action short video of a pet dancing, with realistic cat fur, paw pads, and indoor lighting; features high-quality partial 3D facial deformation effects. Not a static shot or stop-motion: the cat continuously twists, jumps, and moves its paws in rhythm throughout the video, with expression effects embedded in the dance.

[Duration]
8.08 seconds, 24fps, 9:16 aspect ratio, single long take with a fixed low camera angle, no editing or zooming.

[Scene]
A warm home bedroom. The cat stands on pink bedding/mattress, shot from a low, slightly low angle; background has gray-green curtains on the left, a gray folding chair in the middle, and a warm brown wooden cabinet on the right. Warm yellow indoor light, the frame is slightly tilted, and the background remains fixed.

[Character]
A realistic fluffy cat based on the reference image. The cat stands on its hind legs to dance, with its upper body swaying continuously and its front paws making dance gestures; actions are exaggerated but the fur, legs, paws, tail, and lighting must remain realistic. Only one cat in the frame, no human hands, no text, no watermarks.

[Rhythm and Motion]
The cat does not stop to make expressions; instead, every movement has a beat: the body bounces up and down to the rhythm, shoulders and head shake, and paws follow continuous trajectories. Expression changes happen during the dance. Each deformation quickly rebounds and immediately transitions into the next dance gesture.

[00:00-00:00.50] Dance Intro
The cat stands straight, swaying slightly and bouncing up and down. Its paws rise alternately from the chest, finally touching the cheeks and corners of the mouth with eyes looking at the camera in a cute opening pose.

[00:00.50-00:01.12] Mouth-Pulling Dance
The cat continues to twist its waist, paws grabbing the corners of its mouth and pulling them sideways. The mouth becomes an ultra-wide transverse shape with the tongue slightly showing; eyes squint. Key: the cat pulls its own mouth while dancing, not self-deformation.

[00:01.12-00:01.92] Head-Holding Sway
The cat releases, the mouth snaps back to normal. Paws circle above the head; body sways left and right, closing eyes for a beat then opening wide, paws moving continuously.

[00:01.92-00:02.50] Chin-Cradling Tilt
Paws slide to the chin and cheeks, body tilts left and then back to the center in two small side sways. Round eyes and closed mouth for an innocent, coquettish expression.

[00:02.50-00:03.00] Prep Jump
The cat bounces up from the chin cradle, paws back to the head, eyes wide open preparing for the next beat.

[00:03.00-00:03.55] Vertical Stretching Scare Dance
While holding its head, the cat jumps up. The head, neck, and upper body are suddenly stretched vertically like an elastic rubber cat; eyes become huge white ovals with small dot pupils, and the mouth forms an 'O' shape. The cat continues to bounce while stretched.

[00:03.55-00:04.30] Full 360 Spin
The cat snaps back to normal, paws tucked at the chest, performing a full rotation. It shows its profile, then the full tabby back and tail, then the other side, ending back at the camera. The rotation is seamless and complete.

[00:04.30-00:04.75] Single Paw Beat
Immediately after the spin, the cat leans back slightly, lifting its left front paw straight up to reveal the pink pad clearly while the other paw is tucked.

[00:04.75-00:05.30] Pouty Head Sway
The raised paw returns to the head arc. The cat shakes its head, shrugs slightly, with droopy sad eyes and a small closed mouth, dancing a 'pitiful' routine.

[00:05.30-00:06.10] Cheek-Pointing Smile
Paws drop to the cheeks, pointing inward; the body sways while the cheeks puff out. Eyes go from droopy to squinty, mouth slowly stretching into an exaggerated satisfied smile.

[00:06.10-00:06.75] Pink Pad Laugh
On a strong beat, both paws open toward the camera to show pink pads; the body jumps. The face widens horizontally into an exaggerated laugh showing tiny fangs and a pink tongue.

[00:06.75-00:07.35] Recovery Twist
The face returns to normal. Paws alternate at the chest in a cross-motion dance; the body continues to twist with a calm gaze.

[00:07.35-00:07.70] Rose Dance Entry
The cat reaches out one paw. A real deep red rose enters from the bottom left; the cat accurately grabs the green stem while moving.

[00:07.70-00:08.08] Rose Dance Finale
Holding the vertical rose, the cat tilts right and sways. It closes its eyes and sticks out its pink tongue in an intoxicated, funny laughing expression. The video ends on the dancing cat holding the rose with its tongue out.

[Special Effect Restrictions]
The mouth stretches only when paws grab it; vertical stretching only when paws hold the head; the spin must show the full back and tail; the rose must enter from bottom left and be caught. The dance must be continuous with no static posing throughout. 9:16

Cinematic realistic texture, pure ancient Chinese xianxia aesthetics. Style requirements: Restrained emotional drama transitioning into warm, deadpan humor. Elegant classical character blocking, Arri Alexa cinematic texture, stable facial micro-details, fine film grain, natural volumetric light. Core structure: 'Three-Beat Emotional Reversal'. 1st beat: use a cold remark to create emotional drop. 2nd beat: character's actions contradict the remark. 3rd beat: a weighty line redefines the relationship. Strict rule: plot must be driven by character choices, dialogue, and action; environment remains neutral and non-intervening.

II. Narrative Principles
The core is the re-confirmation of the relationship, not superficial conflict. Tone: quiet, restrained, with slight misunderstanding in the first half; warm and unsentimental in the second half. Humor comes from their mutual understanding and the senior sister's blunt way of caring.

III. Reference Control
1. Character Anchors: @Image 1 strictly for Senior Sister (Role A). @Image 2 strictly for Junior Sister (Role B).
2. Environment: Merge uploaded backgrounds into a unified geography. 推演Terrain, architecture, scale, materials, vegetation, weather, lighting, etc. to create a consistent new space shared across three shots.

IV. Character Settings
Role A (Senior Sister): Same as @Image 1. 25-30 years old, East Asian, oval face, fair skin, dark almond eyes, black hair partially pinned with white jade, tall and slender. Outfit: white embroidered silk hanfu, wide sleeves, silver belt, jade pendant, white boots. Holds a silver longsword.
Role B (Junior Sister): Same as @Image 2. 20-25 years old, round lively face, braided black hair, petite. Outfit: celadon linen hanfu, dark belt, wooden hairpin, black shoes. Holds a dark steel sword. Extra: Right wrist wrapped in clean light-colored cloth (must be stable throughout).

V. Environmental Principles
Environment operates independently and naturally (wind, water flow, mist, reflections) but does not trigger or resolve the plot. It only provides realism and depth.

VI. Prop Continuity
Dark steel sword, wrist wrap, and the cloth used to wrap the sword must be consistent. The wrapping action must be detailed and sincere, as it serves as the evidence for the second beat reversal.

VII. Storyboard Script
0-5s | Wide Shot: In a quiet resting space, the Junior Sister looks at her sword and asks: 'Senior Sister, what if I can no longer hold the sword?' The white-clad Senior Sister answers without hesitation: 'Then don't hold it.' Beat 1 must feel cold, creating a drop for the character and audience.
5-10s | Medium Shot: Junior Sister is visibly hurt, saying: 'You are certainly blunt.' Senior Sister doesn't explain but takes the sword and carefully wraps it in cloth. She says: 'There are so many paths down the mountain; who says you must fly with a sword?' Beat 2 shows her actions contradict her words—she is protecting her sister's future.
10-15s | Close-up: Junior Sister asks: 'Am I still your junior sister?' Senior Sister looks her in the eye: 'It's you I recognize, not this sword.' A weighty pause. Junior Sister smiles slightly and asks: 'Will you still scold me then?' Sister replies: 'Yes, as always.' Junior Sister laughs, and the Sister hides a tiny smile while continuing to wrap the sword. Beat 3 redefines the relationship with warmth and deadpan humor.

VIII-XII. Performance & Technical
Detailed acting cues for facial expressions, hand movements for wrapping the sword, cinematic Arri Alexa camera movement (16:9), native Mandarin dialogue sync, and high technical fidelity for silk fabrics and micro-expressions.

title: Traditional Japanese Ukiyo-e Scroll Animation
description: An elaborate prompt for generating a woodblock-print style video in Seedance 2.5, featuring a traditional Japanese scroll that unrolls to reveal a living ukiyo-e city scene with specific instructions for texture, color palette, and transitions.
promptText: [SUMMARY] 15 seconds, 16:9, 24fps. A Japanese emakimono picture scroll unrolls from right to left, the ukiyo-e woodblock city painted on it comes alive, and the film lands on Mount Fuji with a title on the blank paper. Animated woodblock-print style. One single slow leftward drift carries the entire film. [GLOBAL SETUP] Look and texture: 2D animated Japanese ukiyo-e woodblock print. Flat hand-printed color, visible woodgrain, washi paper fibre showing through every surface, thin sumi-ink outlines, gold-leaf cloud bands, Rinpa-school decorative flatness. Keep the ink lines slightly uneven, the way a hand-cut block prints. Palette: washi ivory, indigo ai-iro, vermilion shu-iro, gold kin-iro, golden-yellow yamabuki-iro, pine-green matsu-midori, sumi black. No other colors. The scroll as an object: the ivory washi paper of the scroll, with its dark wooden roller, stays visible at the top and bottom of the frame from 0 to 2.5s and again from 11.5 to 15.0s. Between 2.5 and 11.5s the camera is inside the painting and the paper edges are out of frame. Camera language: exactly one camera move per time slice, always small amplitude at slow speed. The overall direction of travel is leftward for the whole film. Never combine two camera moves in one slice. No handheld shake. Transitions: use zoom-in transition at 2.5s, ink-wash transition at 5.0s, matching-shape transition at 7.5s, and zoom-out transition at 12.5s. No hard cuts anywhere. Nothing appears out of empty space. Keep the camera's breathing in harmony with the length of each slice and leave enough time for each transition to complete. Forbidden throughout: no subtitles, no background music, no photorealism, no 3D rendering, no CG lighting, no video-game look, no modern buildings, no trains, no cars, no power lines, no neon, no Japanese kanji or kana characters anywhere in the frame, no watermark, no logo, no on-screen text at all before 12.5s, no mosaic, no tiling, no puzzle-piece assembly, no rapid cutting. [TIMELINE] 0-2.5s — The scroll opens Scene: A closed emakimono scroll with a dark wooden roller sits at the right edge of an ivory frame. Action: The scroll unrolls leftward and reveals a painted Nihonbashi Bridge. The painted crowd on the bridge starts to move and walks across it. A painted boat slides out from under the bridge and its flat ink outlines ripple into moving water. Camera: slow leftward drift, small amplitude, following the unrolling paper. Sound: paper rustling, a wooden roller turning, then a low market crowd fading in. Not in this slice: no text, no music, no camera shake. 2.5-5.0s — Into the painting: the food street Transition: zoom-in transition. The camera pushes into the painted surface until the paper edges leave the frame and the painting fills the whole screen. Scene: An open-air Edo food street under fluttering vermilion nobori banners. Action: A chef presses a piece of nigiri sushi between his hands and sets it down on a bare wooden board. Steam lifts from a soba pot as a cook draws noodles out of the water. A customer pulls a noren curtain aside and steps in under it. Camera: slow push in, small amplitude, stopping on the sushi board. Sound: a knife tapping wood, oil sizzling, a pot bubbling, cloth brushing. Not in this slice: no text, no music, no modern kitchen equipment. 5.0-7.5s — The river Transition: ink-wash transition. Sumi ink bleeds across the frame like ink dropped in water, and the river scene emerges out of the bleed. Scene: The Sumida River, an arched wooden bridge, rows of low wooden townhouses on the far bank under gold cloud bands. Action: A boatman pushes his pole and the boat glides forward past the bridge. Cherry blossom petals blow across the water from the right. A woman in a patterned kimono standing on the bridge turns her head and looks toward the camera. Camera: slow leftward tracking shot, small amplitude, keeping pace with the boat. Sound: an oar dipping, wood creaking, water lapping, wind through cherry branches. Not in this slice: no text, no music, no motorboats. 7.5-9.5s — Night, lanterns, kabuki Transition: matching-shape transition. A round pink cherry petal drifting in the previous slice matches into a round red paper lantern in this one. Scene: A night street of two-story wooden machiya townhouses under a deep indigo sky. Action: Red paper lanterns light up one after another down both sides of the street. A kabuki theater curtain sways open at the far end and an actor in bold red kumadori face paint strikes a still mie pose. Camera: slow tilt up, small amplitude, from the lanterns to the sky above the rooftops. Sound: wooden kabuki clappers striking twice, geta sandals on plank streets, a low crowd. Not in this slice: no text, no music, no electric light. 9.5-12.5s — Fireworks and the whole city Continuous from the previous slice, the tilt up carries straight into this one. Scene: Golden fireworks open in the indigo sky above the river. Action: Two fireworks bloom and fall in gold and vermilion. The view widens into one grand bird's-eye folding-screen painting of the whole city of Edo across the full width of the frame: dense wooden rooftops, winding canals, arched bridges, boat traffic, a vermilion torii gate, a temple complex, and the tiered white keep of Edo Castle, with gold-leaf cloud bands drifting between the districts. At 11.5s the ivory washi paper edges of the scroll slide back in at the top and bottom, revealing the whole city to be one continuous painting on one scroll. Camera: slow pull out, large amplitude, one single continuous move. Sound: fireworks booming and crackling far away, the crowd noise widening and thinning into open air. Not in this slice: no text, no music, no shattering or reassembling of the image. 12.5-15.0s — Mount Fuji and the title Transition: zoom-out transition completing into the far end of the scroll. Scene: Snow-capped Mount Fuji stands alone on the right against a gold sky. Wide empty ivory washi paper fills the left half of the frame. Action: Cherry blossom petals drift down across the empty paper. The single large word "EDO" fades in on that empty paper in clean pale sumi-black geometric sans-serif capitals. One beat later the smaller line "NOW CALLED TOKYO" fades in directly beneath it. Both lines are English Latin capitals, spelled exactly as written here, centered on the empty paper, sharp and perfectly legible, with no Japanese characters, no extra words and no misspellings. The two lines are static once they appear and are not re-rendered. Camera: the drift comes to rest and holds perfectly still for the last 1.5 seconds. Sound: a single distant temple bell ringing once, then quiet wind. Not in this slice: no music, no additional text, no camera movement after the title appears. [CLOSING CONSTRAINTS] Throughout the whole film: keep the flat ukiyo-e woodblock look, the washi paper fibre, the seven-color palette and the uneven hand-cut ink lines identical from the first frame to the last. Keep every camera move small in amplitude and slow in speed, and keep the overall direction of travel leftward. Keep all transitions soft, with no hard cuts and nothing appearing out of empty space. Throughout the whole film: no subtitles, no background music, no photorealism, no 3D rendering, no modern objects of any kind, no Japanese kanji or kana characters, no watermark and no logo. title: Ancient Swordsman Duel Face-off
description: A highly structured cinematic prompt for Seedance 2.0 depicting an intense visual duel between two ancient Chinese female swordsmen in a movie-quality style.
promptText:
Seedance Prompt | Turn an Intense Duel of Gazes into a High-Level Martial Arts Showdown

I. Project Positioning
Cinematic realistic texture, pure ancient Chinese xianxia aesthetics. 
Overall style: Epic-level master duel camera grammar, restrained visual comedy, Arri Alexa cinematic quality, clear and stable facial micro-details, fine film grain, natural volumetric light, ample controlled quiet pauses, and precise rhythmic response.
Core Plot: Two true masters take a mundane act of 'staring at each other' and escalate it into a contest of martial dignity.
Hard Limits: No magic failures, no secret reveals, no environmental accidents, no clumsy character moments. All humor must stem from pride, competitive desire, micro-expressions, breathing, and rhythm.

II. Narrative Principles
Plot progression relies solely on: Intention, gaze, breathing, micro-expressions, pauses, rhythm, dialogue, and minimal physical reactions. 
The environment must remain a vivid, active, and neutral world with continuous physical changes like flowing water, drifting mountain fog, swaying vegetation, shifting light, and natural parallax.

III. Reference Control
1. Character Anchors: @Image 1 for the Sword Immortal Senior Sister, @Image 2 for the Junior Sister.
2. Environment Reference: New uploaded backgrounds define the environment DNA, organized into a unified new space that respects identity and logic across three shots.

IV. Character Settings
- Character A: Sword Immortal Senior Sister (@Image 1). 25–30 year old East Asian female, oval face, white embroidered silk hanfu, silver belt, jade pendant, carrying a silver longsword (sheathed).
- Character B: Junior Sister (@Image 2). 20–25 year old East Asian female, round face, green linen hanfu, dark belt, carrying a dark steel sword (sheathed).

V. Core Performance Logic
The scene looks like a master duel but is a battle of composure and holding back basic human reactions. Humor comes from the contrast between the small event and the grand ritual.

VI. Storyboard
- 0–5s: Wide/Long shot. Two women stand 3 steps apart in a quiet space, sheathed swords in hand, staring seriously. Sister: "Today we compete in composure, not swords." Junior: "How?" Sister: "Whoever looks away first loses." Junior: "Bring it."
- 5–10s: Medium/Cowboy shot. Symmetrical composition, camera slowly pushes in. No head movement, locked gaze. Junior blinks slightly; Sister raises an eyebrow. Eyes become watery. Junior: "Sister, your eyes are red." Sister: "So are yours."
- 10–15s: Close-up/Extreme Close-up. Focus on eyelashes trembling and water in lower eyelids. They blink simultaneously. Quiet pause. Junior: "You blinked first." Sister: "You spoke first." Pause. Junior: "Draw?" Sister: "Again." Final shot: They lean forward slightly, locking gaze again. Cut to black.

VII. Performance & Movement
Characters remain intelligent and powerful. No exaggerated faces or slapstick. Precise micro-expressions: squinting, eyebrow raising, stable breathing, watery eyes. Minimal head movement.

VIII. Camera & Technical Requirements
16:9 landscape, 3 continuous shots, Arri Alexa look. Restrained camera movement from wide to close-up. Real volumetric depth and physical effects (hair, silk). Synchronized Mandarin dialogue. Seedance 2.0 Fast optimization for identity stability.

title: Fantasy Taoist Warrior and Giant Short
description: A cinematic animated short prompt featuring a young Taoist warrior and her giant partner, emphasizing comedic timing and stylized realism.
promptText:
Create a 30-second cinematic animated short featuring two original fantasy characters: a young female Taoist warrior and her gigantic reluctant giant partner.

Keep the character designs completely consistent throughout the entire video.
Scene 1, 0-5s: The New Target
Begin with a quiet atmospheric mountain landscape.
A gentle mountain breeze passes through the frame. The camera slowly tilts downward, revealing the top of a large woven bamboo conical hat [from the reference image]
The girl's long dark hair moves naturally in the wind beneath the hat. The camera continues slowly downward until her face [from the reference image] is revealed.
She looks completely calm and slightly annoyed.
She picks up the phone and says in a casual, matter-of-fact voice:
"He's the new target? Got it."
She rolls her eyes.
Subtle wind, distant birds, soft mountain ambience, cinematic silence before the dialogue.
Scene 2, 5-11s: The Reluctant Partner
Cut to a dramatic wide shot.
The female Taoist stands on the edge of a huge mountain cliff [from the reference image]. Vast mountains, mist and clouds stretch into the distance.
Behind her, the gigantic blue-gray stone-skinned giant [from the reference image] is crouching on the ground, taking a rest. His enormous body towers over the landscape.
She casually turns toward him and says:

The giant slowly raises his head with an exhausted expression.
He looks deeply annoyed.
"I haven't rested enough yet!"
His voice is deep and powerful, but his expression should feel more like an exhausted coworker complaining about overtime than an angry monster.
The Taoist remains completely unfazed.

The vehicle disappears down the mountain road, leaving a small cloud of exhaust and dust drifting directly into his face.
He slowly wipes the dust from his face with an irritated expression.
Comedic timing, exaggerated facial animation, but grounded physical movement.

title: Fitness Influencer Gym Vlog
description: A realistic handheld DV camcorder aesthetic prompt for a late-night gym vlog featuring a fitness influencer and detailed shot breakdown.
promptText:
CAMERA:
Realistic handheld DV camcorder aesthetic. A glamorous European brunette fitness influencer films herself in selfie and first-person style. Natural hand shake, slight framing imperfections, autofocus shifts, subtle zooms, occasional motion blur. Mix handheld selfie shots with a few fixed external angles using clean jump cuts. Never show the camera or her setting it up.

LOOK:
Soft vintage DV tape character, slight blur and tape noise, mild highlight bloom, subtle exposure flicker, muted contrast, realistic skin texture and natural indoor gym lighting.

STYLE:
Realistic late-night fitness vlog, playful, confident, slightly flirty and breathless. It should feel self-recorded and spontaneous rather than like a commercial. Fast clean cuts, natural body language and strong continuity.

CHARACTER:
Beautiful glamorous European brunette woman in her mid-20s, brown almond-shaped eyes, long lashes, glossy lips, sculpted features, lightly tanned glowing skin and thick dark-brown hair in a high ponytail. Slim, feminine athletic figure. Soft-glam makeup, fitted long-sleeve athletic crop top, high-waisted leggings, white sneakers and a towel around her neck or shoulder. No jewelry.

SETTING:
Quiet modern gym late at night with mirrors, dumbbell rack, bench, stretching mat and water bottle. Warm overhead lighting, mostly empty, calm atmosphere. No trainer or other people.

CONTINUITY:
Keep the exact same woman, face, hair, outfit, body and environment throughout. No extra people, duplicated limbs, broken hands, disappearing objects or impossible movements. No visible camera or camera setup.

STORYBOARD — 30 SECONDS / 10 CUTS:

1. (~3s) Arm’s-length selfie. She walks through the empty gym, slightly breathless but smiling. “Okay... late-night gym vlog.”

2. (~3s) Handheld pan across dumbbells, mirrors and empty floor, then back to her. “It’s basically empty in here.”

3. (~3s) Mirror selfie. She adjusts her ponytail, looks at herself and smirks. “I look tired, but we’re still doing this.”

4. (~3s) Fixed medium shot. Jump cut to her already beside the bench. She picks up dumbbells and gets ready. No dialogue.

5. (~3s) Same fixed shot. She performs controlled dumbbell presses, then lowers the weights and smiles. “That woke me up fast.”

6. (~3s) Walking selfie with towel over one shoulder, breathing harder. “Upper body done... and I’m already dying.”

7. (~3s) Tight handheld close-up. She drinks from the water bottle and exhales. “Best part of the workout.”

8. (~3s) Fixed wider shot facing the mirror. She stretches, briefly poses playfully and laughs. “A little stretch so I can pretend I’m disciplined.”

9. (~3s) Close selfie. Slightly flushed, she brushes back her hair and smiles tiredly. “I always say quick workout... and then stay forever.”

10. (~3s) Final arm’s-length selfie as she walks toward the exit, waves and smiles. “Okay, I’m done. Good night.”

FINAL:
Make it feel like an authentic self-recorded late-night gym vlog.

title: Snowy Night Xianxia Combat Sequence

promptText:
A 25-second continuous live-action martial arts special effects fight video. The overall style uses frosty night cold blue moonlight, grey-white snow reflection, bluish-black brick walls, and dark orange firelight from grey pit charcoal as a cold-warm contrast, low saturation but bright and transparent; ARRI Alexa film texture, 35mm ultra-wide-angle lens, delicate 35mm film grain. Textures of real skin, wet hair, coarse cloth, bricks, snow, wooden beams, incense ash, and a small amount of sparks. The overall combat logic refers to the close-combat martial arts design of Hong Kong hard-boiled action blockbusters: emphasizing close-quarters pressure, continuous offensive, counter-moves into grappling, impact into throwing, short-range combat, environment-based combos, and clear cause-and-effect of movements. Not a floating Xianxia fight, but a high-intensity continuous death battle of 'real combat logic + exaggerated martial arts special effects.'
Theme: Pursuit Battle in a Snowy Night Mortuary.
The protagonist is a female martial artist, age about 35 to 45, Chinese female, lean and strong build, thin but powerful shoulders and back, strong explosive power, fierce, short, and fast movements, a practical martial arts expert. Cold face, calm and dangerous eyes, long hair tied up or half-tied, with a few stray wet strands allowed. Outfit is deep cyan-grey or black-grey old-style martial arts short-cut suit, suitable for close combat, wearing narrow-leg pants and cloth leggings, old cloth shoes or lightweight leather boots. Weapon is a 'dark iron short ruler', slightly shorter than the forearm, held with one hand, capable of parrying, hitting, smashing, wrist-locking, and knife-trapping, also cooperating with the other hand for grappling control. The protagonist's core technique is 'Bridge-Locking and Momentum-Breaking,' with the core strategy of staying close to the center line, intercepting weapons, controlling arms, continuous elbow and knee strikes, shoulder and back ramming, grappling and throwing, and then finishing with the short ruler. Afterimages/instant steps are only auxiliary footwork for rushing, repositioning, line-dodging, and back-taking, not to overshadow the combat.
The opponent is a 48-year-old Skin-Borrower, a humanoid fox demon, with withered yellow long hair, a face like a layer of loose old skin, wearing a clay yellow short robe, holding a normal short knife. Skilled in Yellow Wind Claw Pressure, close-range knife strikes, shoulder ramming, low-level sliding pounce, and afterimage pouncing. Movements are sinister, change lines quickly, and are poisonous at close range, like a fierce martial arts bandit using a knife, but with a slight demonic aura.
The scene is the courtyard of a mountain mortuary on a snowy night: snow-covered stone flat, incense burning pit, corpse-storing corridor, black wood coffin racks, corpse-washing stone table, withered cypress, and narrow stone steps in the back. Spatial relationships must be clear: center is the snow flat; left is the incense pit; right is the stone table and coffin racks; corridors, pillars, and beams on all sides; stone steps and brick walls in the back. Cold blue moonlight falls from above and the side-back, while charcoal in the pit provides flickering dark orange light, creating cold-warm lighting. Snow powder, ash, cold mist, and sparks float in the air.
General Movement Principles: The entire film must have continuous martial arts action and clear combat logic, with a valid movement change every 0.4 to 0.8 seconds: attack, parry, dodge, grapple, counter, throw, explosion. No standing and charging power, no slow posing, no light-weight flying. All moves must be based on real body power: kicking off the ground, turning the hips, dropping the shoulders, cutting the line, staying close, locking the wrist, sealing the elbow, knee-striking, tripping, using walls, pillars, tables, and coffin racks. The combat feel should be like a real bone-breaking close battle but with exaggerated martial arts effects.

title: Manhattan Street Cinematic Chase
description: A high-tension cinematic one-take pursuit prompt for Seedance 2.0, set in a realistic Manhattan street environment with complex camera work.
promptText:
Duration: 15 seconds
Aspect Ratio: 16:9 landscape
Style: Cinematic Chase Oner, New York Manhattan street, cloudy diffused natural light, cold tone low-saturation documentary film quality.

Character: Protagonist

I. Narrative Goals
The entire video is a continuous horizontal side-tracking long shot. The camera remains parallel to the street, moving left in a shoulder-mounted stabilizer posture, without cutting or changing position. 
1. Front: Tracking the running female lead to build speed and tension.
2. Middle: Briefly losing the subject due to foreground obstruction, with hesitant camera movement before locating pursuers.
3. Back: Focus shifts from pursuers to the distant female lead; camera recaptures and accelerates.

II. Spatial Layers
Foreground: Parked cars, passing yellow taxis, newsstands, construction scaffolding. 
Subject Layer: Running female lead -> Pursuers -> Female lead.
Mid-ground: Outdoor restaurant seating, startled passersby, men in navy suits rushing out of revolving doors.
Background: Manhattan main street vanishing point, traffic lights, white steam from vents.

III. Executable Camera Timeline
- 00:00-00:01.8: Establish Stillness. Slow left pan focusing on an old man at an outdoor table.
- 00:01.8-00:02.3: Triggered. Female lead rushes past; camera snaps into a leftward acceleration with realistic shake.
- 00:02.3-00:06: Tracking Speed. Medium-close side shot of the lead at full sprint. Background is blurred. Focus on her tense expression and heavy travel bag.
- 00:06-00:07.2: Obstruction. A yellow taxi blocks the view; camera loses the subject.
- 00:07.2-00:08.3: Hesitation. Camera slows and drifts right to find the subject, eventually locking onto men in suits exiting a building.
- 00:08.3-00:11.5: Pursuers. Tracking three men in navy suits running through the crowd.
- 00:11.5-00:12.5: Focus Drift. Focus shifts from pursuers to the distant female lead; camera accelerates again.
- 00:12.5-00:15: Convergence. Camera tracks the lead entering a dense crowd. She is exhausted. Final shot holds as she disappears into the crowd.

Character aura is solemn and oppressive.

Both people fully and clearly visible from shoes to head.

The two swords first collide precisely, making a single crisp 'clang'.
Then complete two clean, elegant, easily identifiable swordplay exchanges.

Gripping swords

Body posture

title: K-pop Flash Mob Music Video
description: A comprehensive prompt for generating a continuous 30-second music video featuring a K-pop dancer in Seoul, with specific audio and movement instructions.
promptText: Landscape iPhone video, one unbroken 30-second take, no cuts. LOCATION / TIME Hongdae, Seoul, blue hour. The pavement is still wet from rain. Neon signage is just starting to come on. Use a long, straight stretch of shopfront-lined sidewalk with enough clear depth for the performer and camera to travel roughly 40 meters continuously. SOUNDTRACK This is a music video. The track is the entire audio. The music is NOT playing inside the scene. It is a finished studio recording laid directly over the footage in the edit, exactly like a professional music-video soundtrack. The music must be: - Clean - Loud - Full-range - Mastered - Immediate and front-of-mix - Filling the entire frequency spectrum, including deep sub frequencies Music style: K-pop dance-break instrumental at around 104 BPM. Musical elements: - Hard 808 sub - Tight, snappy claps - Sparse minor-key synth stabs - Layered female vocal ad-libs - Stacked vocal hooks with no intelligible words Energy progression: The track begins sparse and restrained, then transitions into a full drop that carries the entire second half. IMPORTANT AUDIO RESTRICTIONS: NO street ambience. NO traffic noise. NO footsteps. NO crowd noise. NO voices. NO wind. NO environmental sound. NO room reverb. NO outdoor echo on the music. The soundtrack must NOT sound like: - A phone speaker - A car stereo - A busking speaker - Music playing from a nearby store - Music heard from across the street No muffling. No distance effect. No bandpass filtering. The music must remain studio-clean, full-frequency, loud, and immediate throughout. THE PERFORMER A Korean woman in her early twenties. Appearance: - High ponytail - Oversized varsity jacket - Cropped tee underneath - Wide black trousers - Chunky sneakers She is a professional working music-video dancer and immediately reads as one through her movement quality. She travels forward for the ENTIRE 30-second take. She dances for the ENTIRE 30-second take. The forward walk itself is choreography. Walking is never used as a break between dance phrases. Movement vocabulary: - Hip-hop bounce with strong, visible knee action - Chest isolations - Rib isolations - Shoulder pops - Waacking arm circles - Sharp wrist snaps - K-pop point-choreography accents - Quick heel-toe footwork incorporated into her traveling steps Movement density: Maintain roughly 4 to 6 clearly visible choreographic accents per second. The movement remains sustained throughout. She NEVER drops into ordinary walking. Every accent should feel rhythmically connected to the soundtrack. Her movement amplitude follows the music: - Smaller and more contained during the sparse opening - Increasingly confident as the track builds - Biggest and most explosive during the final drop Performance behavior: She occasionally half-sings along to the track without producing audible diegetic vocals. She catches the camera lens, grins, breaks eye contact naturally, then reconnects with the lens. She feels confident, playful, spontaneous, and extremely comfortable performing directly to camera. THE CAMERA Handheld iPhone footage. Landscape orientation. One continuous 30-second shot. NO cuts. The camera operator walks backward ahead of the performer for the entire take, matching her forward pace. Camera height: Approximately chest height. Framing: Keep her centered and framed from head to sneakers for most of the take. Use a wide iPhone lens perspective. She must remain large enough in the frame that: - Her face stays clearly resolved - Her eyes remain readable - Her hands remain clearly visible - Her dance details remain easy to understand Camera behavior should feel authentically handheld: - Mild natural hand movement - Slight rolling-shutter wobble - Small framing imperfections - Autofocus hunts once or twice - Exposure subtly adjusts as she passes bright storefronts Wet pavement and asphalt reflect the neon signage and surrounding lights. DO NOT use: - Gimbal smoothness - Orbiting camera movement - Zooms - Camera rotation - Slow motion - Drone shots - Stabilized cinematic tracking CROWD BUILD 0-4 SECONDS The performer dances forward alone. Ordinary pedestrians are already moving naturally through the background and around her. Nobody appears to know what is about to happen. 4-9 SECONDS One guy who is already visible behind her begins catching the groove. He starts copying her shoulder choreography approximately half a beat late. His participation should initially feel accidental rather than staged. 9-15 SECONDS Three or four additional people gradually join. Each dancer must peel naturally out of the existing pedestrian flow. Entrances can come from: - The left side of the sidewalk - A visible shopfront - Further behind the performer - Other positions already established within the shot Nobody should suddenly materialize or enter from an impossible location. Each person was already somewhere logically present within the continuous environment. 15-21 SECONDS The group grows to approximately 12 to 15 dancers behind her. They remain loosely packed rather than forming a perfect formation. They copy her accents with slight ripple delays. The timing differences should make the sequence feel spontaneous and contagious rather than perfectly rehearsed. 21-30 SECONDS The number of dancers now HOLDS. Do not keep adding more people. Instead, increase the energy. The group gradually tightens into a loose wedge formation behind the lead performer. Choreographic intensity reaches its peak. The lead performer remains the unmistakable visual focus. FINAL 2 SECONDS She throws her hardest, sharpest choreographic accent directly toward the camera lens. Everyone behind her lands the same beat with her. The movement hits hard and feels satisfying. The shot does NOT freeze. The dancers remain physically alive after the accent. Bodies continue breathing and settling naturally as the 30-second frame ends. BACKGROUND PEDESTRIANS Some pedestrians NEVER join the choreography. They continue walking normally around the dancers. Their reactions vary naturally: - Slightly annoyed - Curious - Amused - Indifferent Some carefully edge around the growing dance group while continuing toward their destination. This contrast between dancers and uninvolved pedestrians is essential for making the moment feel real. PHYSICAL REALISM Grounded human biomechanics throughout. Every movement must show: - Visible weight transfer - Proper foot planting - Real momentum - Believable balance - Natural joint articulation - Correct body mechanics No sliding feet. No floating. No impossible limb motion. No rubbery joints. No unnatural acceleration. No teleporting people. No duplicated pedestrians. The lead performer stays the clear focus throughout the entire take. Maintain enough proximity and image clarity that her face, hands, expressions, clothing, and choreography stay clearly resolved even with the wide lens.

title: Cinematic Xianxia Apology Drama
description: A comprehensive multi-scene script for a cinematic Xianxia video involving a comedic and prideful apology between two martial arts sisters with specific character consistency controls.
promptText:
Seedance Prompt | Dual-way Stubborn Apology Reversal

I. Project Positioning

Movie-level photorealistic quality, pure ancient Chinese Xianxia aesthetics, restrained relational comedy, elegant classical character blocking, Arri Alexa cinematic texture, clear and stable facial details, fine film grain, and natural volumetric lighting.

The core reversal of this segment is:
Two very proud people both actually want to apologize first, but neither is willing to admit they are apologizing.

The plot can only be driven by the characters' own intentions, dialogue, actions, and rhythm.
The environment is always an independently running, real-existing living world, but it must remain narratively neutral: does not actively trigger plot, solve problems, change character goals, create reversals, or express emotions for the characters.

II. Reference Controls
1. Character Reference
@Image 1: Used only as the identity anchor for Character ID A, the Sword Immortal Senior Sister.
@Image 2: Used only as the identity anchor for Character ID B, the Junior Sister.

2. Environmental Reference
All newly uploaded background and location reference images jointly determine the same environmental DNA. Before formal composition, silently deduce and integrate: actual terrain, architectural language, spatial scale, material age, vegetation ecology, water system flow, weather state, cloud and mist density, main light direction, reflection relationships, overall color system, atmospheric depth, and real walkable routes. Then recombine into a unique, complete, and unified new space that has never appeared before.

III. Character Settings
Character ID A | Sword Immortal Senior Sister
Same @Image 1 sister. 25–30 year old East Asian female, oval face, fair natural skin tone, dark almond eyes, black long hair half-tied with a white jade hairpin, tall and slender.
Always wears the same outfit: white embroidered silk Hanfu, semi-transparent layered wide sleeves, silver waistband, jade pendant, white cloth boots. Carries a unique silver longsword.

Character ID B | Junior Sister
Same @Image 2 sister. 20–25 year old East Asian female, rounded and lively face, black hair braided, petite stature.
Always wears the same outfit: bluish-green linen Hanfu, dark belt, wooden hairpin, black cloth shoes. Carries a unique dark steel sword.

IV. Core Props
The following props must be kept strictly consistent throughout:
One unique white jade sword tassel, one unique repaired white wrist guard, Character A's silver sword, Character B's dark steel sword.

V. Storyboard Script
0–5s | Wide or Long Shot
In the location replanned according to the reference images, the same two women walk from opposite directions and stop three steps apart. Clearly having just had a quarrel, both intentionally avoid direct eye contact. The same white-clothed sister silently places the jade sword tassel on the stone surface between them, saying in a deliberately cold tone: 'Your tassel was too old yesterday, it affects your swordplay.' Almost simultaneously, the same green-clothed junior sister also places the repaired white wrist guard next to it, answering stiffly: 'Your wrist guard was also torn, it affects your drawing of the sword.'
Requirements: Both visible from head to toe, spatial relationship clear, sense of awkwardness after a fight explicit.

5–10s | Medium or Cowboy Shot
Maintain same characters, outfits, items, and geography. Both glance at the item the other put down, then immediately look away as if nothing happened. The white-clothed woman pushes the tassel two inches closer, saying calmly: 'I just happened to change it.' The green-clothed woman also pushes the wrist guard back, answering: 'I also just happened to sew it.' Pause for a beat. The moment the white-clothed woman reaches for the wrist guard, the junior sister also reaches for the tassel; their hands almost touch, then both quickly withdraw and pretend to look at distant scenery.

10–15s | Close-up or Extreme Close-up
The junior sister finally picks up the tassel and ties it to her dark steel sword, whispering: 'So... about yesterday?' The senior sister lowers her head to tie the wrist guard, not looking up, answering calmly: 'What about it?' The junior sister pauses, finally understands, and answers: 'Nothing.' They look at each other briefly for the first time. Extreme close-up: The senior sister notices the junior sister tied the tassel backward; she silently reaches out to turn it the right way, then immediately pulls back. The junior sister tries to suppress a smile, whispering: 'You just never speak properly.' The sister answers almost inaudibly: 'As long as you understand.'

VI. Technical Specs
Total duration: 15 seconds. Aspect ratio: 16:9 landscape. Three continuous clear shots. Native synchronized Mandarin dialogue. Lip-sync precise with dialogue. No subtitles. Only two visible characters throughout. Consistency in face, clothing, props, and geography. Real movement in hands, silk, water, and air.

VII. Performance & Blocking
Characters: Both smart, restrained, dignified. Mature stubbornness rather than childish fighting. Intent to apologize is clear but language avoids 'sorry'. Comedy comes from misaligned expression and synchronized action.
Cinematography: Elegant and restrained. Captured moments: caring while not looking, hands touching/withdrawing, correcting the tassel.
Environment: Living but not scene-stealing.

promptText:

title: Dune 4 Cinematic Sci-Fi Trailer
description: A complex cinematic sci-fi trailer montage prompt for Seedance 2.5, featuring detailed shot breakdowns on a desert planet with dynamic camera movements.
promptText: A 15-second cinematic sci-fi epic movie-trailer montage on a vast desert planet, anamorphic widescreen 21:9, ultra-cinematic large-format look, vintage anamorphic lenses, shallow depth of field, thick atmospheric dust haze, strong horizontal lens flares, warm sand-amber highlights against deep teal shadows, filmic grade, fine 35mm grain, monumental awe-inspiring scale, no on-screen text, no watermark. A sequence of hard cuts like a prestige film trailer. THE CAMERA IS ALWAYS IN MOTION: every shot uses a different angle and a different dynamic camera move — aerial dives, low tracking, orbits, crane rises, FPV rushes — always smooth and cinematic, never shaky amateur footage. SHOT 1 (0.0-2.0s): Camera FALLS SLOWLY DOWN through a near-black cloudscape of golden dust and dark teal atmosphere, a soft horizontal anamorphic streak sweeping past, a glowing horizon rotating slowly far below, embers rushing upward past the lens. Then it SLOWLY DISSOLVES (not a cut) into: SHOT 2 (2.0-4.5s): A slow 90-degree ORBITING ARC around a bald, weathered desert leader in coarse pale robes, starting on his profile and swinging to a tight low-angle front view, sun-cracked skin, calm distant gaze; behind him an endless sea of dunes wheels past out of focus in the haze. Warm rim light travels across his face as the camera circles. SHOT 3 (4.5-5.6s): HARD CUT to a fast low AERIAL DRONE SWEEP racing over rippling dunes toward the exposed edge of a colossal ancient metal hull protruding from the sand like a buried mountain ridge; the camera rushes up its slope and crests it, revealing tiny robed figures on the ridge below. Speed and scale. SHOT 4 (5.6-6.6s): HARD CUT to a hooded engineer-priestess on a pure black background: the camera DESCENDS ON A CRANE from above her head to eye level while slowly circling, one hard side light raking across her as she raises a small glowing amber relic in both hands, dust motes swirling through the beam. Chiaroscuro in motion. SHOT 5 (6.6-7.5s): HARD CUT to a GROUND-LEVEL SKIMMING SHOT: the camera races just above the desert floor through darkness toward a lone robed figure, loose sand grains jumping and vibrating past the lens as the ground trembles, then the camera TILTS UP the figure's silhouette. Low, fast, ominous. SHOT 6 (7.5-8.6s): HARD CUT to an FPV RUSH along a crack tearing open through the desert floor: the camera flies low and fast following the running fracture as dunes avalanche inward on both sides, geysers of sand venting past the lens, robed crowds scattering on the ridges above, dust rolling. Kinetic, accelerating. SHOT 7 (8.6-9.5s): HARD CUT to a STEADICAM TRACKING SHOT pushing through the fleeing crowd behind the heroine in flowing desert robes as she strides against the flow toward the collapse; mid-shot the camera RISES INTO A CRANE MOVE above the crowd as an immense shadow slides across the dunes and swallows her. SHOT 8 (9.5-10.85s): HARD CUT to an extreme close-up of the heroine's face wrapped in a dark desert scarf, only her eyes and cheekbones lit, a bright circular halo of backlight behind her head, soft anamorphic bokeh; the camera SLOWLY SPIRALS a few degrees around her face as her eyes lift upward, widening with awe at something rising off-screen. Emotional center — the one intimate moment amid the motion. SHOT 9 (10.85-12.4s): HARD CUT to THE REVEAL from a RISING AERIAL: the camera craning up alongside a colossal kilometer-long ancient spaceship as it breaches out of the desert, entire waterfalls of sand cascading off its hull and falling PAST THE LENS, rings of dust blasting outward across the dunes below, the low sun flaring behind its silhouette, tiny human figures dwarfed beneath. The camera keeps climbing with the ship, never static. IMAX-scale. RAPID CLIMAX MONTAGE (12.4-15.0s) — a burst of very short hard cuts, roughly 0.3s each, EVERY CUT FROM A COMPLETELY DIFFERENT ANGLE, camera moving in all of them: 12.4s: TOP-DOWN AERIAL plunging toward rows of engine nozzles igniting one by one through the dust, deep orange glow rushing up at the lens. 13.1s: LOW SIDE TRACKING SHOT racing beside a wall-like shockwave of sand as it overtakes silhouetted onlookers on a ridge. 13.6s: EXTREME LOW ANGLE from the desert floor, the ship's silhouette climbing across the sun, lens flare knifing across the frame as the camera tilts up after it. 13.8s: ORBITAL SHOT whipping around the blinding column of thruster fire and sand beneath the rising hull. 14.1s: FPV THROUGH DEBRIS: torn plating and streaming sand whipping past the lens in slow-building force as the camera threads between them. 14.55s: the camera PULLS BACK FAST as the whole frame washes into a glowing golden-red haze of dust and engine fire, the trailer peaks. 15.0s: fade toward black. Consistency: one coherent desert-planet world, one warm-amber-and-teal anamorphic grade, constant fine film grain and dust haze in every shot, monumental scale, prestige-trailer pacing that accelerates into the final montage; the camera never locks off — every shot has smooth cinematic motion and its own distinct angle. Photoreal, no cartoon look, no captions, no logos. Audio: deep sub-bass "braam" trailer horns building in intensity, a low ominous choir swelling, constant desert wind, deep tectonic rumble growing under shots 5-7, then a NEAR-TOTAL SILENCE for half a second just before the reveal — only wind and one heartbeat — followed by a colossal metallic groan and roar as the ship breaches, cascading sand hiss, a sharp sub-bass impact hit on every hard cut, rapid stacked impacts through the climax, full engine thunder at the peak. No dialogue, no lyrics.

promptText:

Highlights are allowed to have slight bloom/halation, presenting a soft glow of sun white, light cherry blossom pink, and pale gold; dark parts remain clean and transparent with a slight cold cyan-blue, no dead black shadows. Color Tone: Low contrast, low saturation, Japanese-style healing palette. The overall color is soft, bright, and airy, with natural and clean skin tones. Cinematographic Texture: Real live-action film cinematography, shallow depth of field, natural focus transitions, slight handheld breathing, and smooth motion shots. Character movements are natural and restrained, and performances express emotions through eyes, breathing, running, pausing, and brief tacit understanding. The imagery should look like a Japanese hot-blooded youth film, rather than anime, illustration, MV, or idol photo books.

Main Character Settings: Character A: Black short-haired male high school student, calm personality, determined eyes. Character B: Slightly curly dark brown short-haired male high school student, direct and flamboyant personality, but not a villain. Character C: Ear-length black short-haired female high school student, the main point guard of the basketball club, and also the main character of the whole film.

Visual Content:
Scene 01 | 0.0–1.5s | Signal Location: School building corridor. Starting Frame: Opens directly with a very close-up shot of Character C's face. She has just finished a fast run, with fine sweat beads on her forehead, short hair clinging to the side of her face, and slightly rapid breathing. She suddenly lifts her eyes, looking sharply off-screen. The background is a real Japanese high school corridor, blurred with a shallow depth of field, showing only faint old window frames, notice boards, worn wall surfaces, and sunset light streaks. Ending Frame: The lens pulls back slightly to a chest-level close-up. Character C holds a basketball in one hand and a blue-purple RAIKU POP plastic bottle in the other. She quickly turns and runs toward the end of the corridor. She wears a white school shirt, a dark pleated skirt, and a black basketball training vest. The surface of the plastic bottle is covered with realistic condensation droplets, and the blue-purple liquid inside sloshes naturally as she runs.

Scene 02 | 1.5–3.0s | Corridor Chase Location: Long school building corridor. Starting Frame: Character C quickly passes through the corridor, with the basketball tucked under one arm and the soda bottle in the other hand. The shot follows from a side low angle, as the sunset forms fast-alternating light and dark bands through continuous windows. Ending Frame: Character A appears from a corner of the corridor, wearing a white short-sleeved school shirt and dark school trousers, catching a basketball rolling in from off-screen. He looks up at Character C, the two have a brief eye contact, then they move toward the stairs simultaneously.

Scene 03 | 3.0–4.5s | Stairs Encounter Location: Narrow concrete stairwell. Starting Frame: Character B runs down quickly from the upper stairs, wearing a white school shirt, a loosened dark tie, and dark school trousers. He dribbles the basketball with one hand and slides his other hand along the metal railing. The shot uses a top-down angle to emphasize the narrow staircase's pressure and movement speed. Ending Frame: Character C appears from the lower stairs and tosses the RAIKU POP soda bottle to Character A. Character A catches the bottle while running, and Character B brushes past them. Both boys must wear school uniforms in this scene, not basketball jerseys.

Scene 04 | 4.5–6.0s | Crossing the Connecting Bridge Location: Covered bridge connecting two school buildings. Starting Frame: Three students enter the bridge from different directions. The lens uses a telephoto compression of the distance between the three, with the background showing real Japanese school building exterior walls, metal window frames, and diagonal sunset light. Ending Frame: The basketball flies at high speed toward the lens, completely blocking the screen, forming a natural circular masking transition.

Scene 05 | 6.0–7.5s | Rooftop Interception Location: School building rooftop. Starting Frame: Character B pushes open the metal rooftop door and catches the basketball in strong backlight. Character A and Character B both wear school uniforms, not basketball jerseys. Character C follows closely out of the door. The corners of their clothes and hair are blown by a strong wind. Ending Frame: Character C cleanly steals the basketball from Character B's hands, quickly turning to dash toward another exit. The camera stays tight on the characters' movement.

Scene 06 | 7.5–9.0s | Entering the Arena Location: Gym entrance and equipment passage. Starting Frame: Character C dashes into the dimly lit gym equipment passage, followed closely by Character A and Character B. The two boys are still wearing white school shirts and trousers. Basketball racks, folding mats, old training equipment, and jersey lockers line the walls. Ending Frame: Character A quickly places the RAIKU POP plastic bottle on an old wooden bench near the gym entrance. The lens focuses first on the product, the bottle vibrating slightly, condensation sliding down, and blue-purple bubbles rising rapidly. In the background, the open entrance to the changing area and hanging basketball jerseys are visible, providing natural spatial cues for the outfit change for the next game.

Scene 07 | 9.0–12.0s | The Final Shot Location: Japanese high school gym basketball court. Clothing Requirement: Only in this formal game do Character A, Character B, and Character C wear full basketball jerseys and shorts. The jerseys belong to the same original campus basketball visual system, mainly in deep navy blue, black, and a small amount of blue-purple. Their jersey numbers are different. Starting Frame: Character C wears a dark basketball jersey and breaks through with a fast dribble. Character A and Character B defend from both sides. The camera follows at high speed close to the wooden floor, shoes making real friction marks and slight wood dust as they stop suddenly. Ending Frame: Character C stops and jumps for a three-pointer. The shot uses a very low angle looking up at her realistic athletic posture as the basketball spins away from her fingertips. The scene uses a match cut to a very close-up of Character A unscrewing the RAIKU POP cap, then immediately cuts back to the basketball cleanly passing through the net. Character A's jersey strap is visible at the edge of his arm, clearly showing he has changed into his game jersey. Lens Language: Ground-level handheld tracking -> Low-angle shot -> Match Cut -> Macro Product Shot -> Net Close-up. Ambient Sound: Continuous dribbling, shoe squeaks, rapid breathing, the 'click' of the bottle cap's tamper-evident ring, the 'pssh' of opening the bottle, the sound of the ball through the net.

Scene 08 | 12.0–15.0s | After-School Boiling Point Location: Indoor rest area outside the gym. Starting Frame: Three students sit on a bench against the wall, still wearing the basketball jerseys and shorts from Scene 07. Character C is in the middle, with Character A and Character B sitting on either side. The background shows the frosted glass gym doors, shoe racks, and jersey hooks. Each of the three drinks from a RAIKU POP blue-purple soda bottle with identical packaging. Three PET plastic bottles clink gently. The characters do not laugh exaggeratedly, only showing fatigue, relief, and a brief tacit understanding. Ending Frame: The screen quickly darkens to a deep navy blue brand background. In the center appears the original fictional brand logo: 'RAIKU POP'. Below it is the Chinese slogan: 'After school, the boiling point is just beginning.'

promptText:

title: 90s Asian Art Movie Cinematic Portrait
description: A comprehensive prompt for creating a 6-second cinematic dynamic portrait of a young woman with a 90s Asian arthouse aesthetic, featuring complex camera movement, depth of field changes, and continuous natural motion.
promptText:
6-second live-action cinematic dynamic portrait, close-up of a young woman, with the damp, hazy, soft-focus aesthetic of 90s Asian art films.

The character is in continuous natural motion throughout, no static posing.

0-2s: The woman is originally lying on her side, face tilted slightly. She naturally raises her head and shoulders while slowly turning to face the camera. As she moves, black long hair slides from her shoulders and cheeks, with a few wet strands brushing across her eyes and lips. Her gaze starts off-camera and naturally follows the camera during the turn.

2-4s: She continues to rise and gently shifts her posture. One hand rises from the bottom of the frame to casually brush away wet hair, fingers sweeping from the temple to the side of the ear. She blinks gently, looking away briefly before meeting the lens again. The hair has noticeable but soft inertial swinging due to movement.

4-6s: The woman moves closer to the camera, her face turning from profile to 3/4 view. Strands of hair continue to slide across her cheeks. Finally, she looks up directly into the camera, movement not yet fully stopped as the frame ends.

Continuous camera movement:
Handheld camera moves in a small arc around the character while slowly approaching; not a fixed position. The shot has slight realistic handheld breathing and spatial parallax. The camera retreats slightly as the character approaches, creating a sense of follow-shooting.

Continuous foreground movement:
Blurred translucent fabric, glass reflections, or plant shadows slowly cross the frame, creating parallax with camera movement. Foreground occasionally obscures half the face before sliding away, creating a voyeuristic sense of candidly capturing the character.

Continuous focus shifting:
85mm, f/1.4, extremely shallow depth of field. Focus is not locked but shifts quickly and softly between eyes, wet hair, and lips as distance changes, simulating a real photographer's manual follow-focus with slight blurring and refocusing.

Shot through damp air and a slightly foggy lens, soft-focus filter, highlights softly blooming, natural halation, low contrast, raised blacks, slightly underexposed, low saturation palette of gray-blue, dark green, and milky white. Moist skin creates soft reflections, and the background melts into abstract blocks of color.

Motion priorities: turning head + rising + hand brushing hair + hair inertia + gaze shifts + camera arc movement + foreground crossing + continuous follow-focus, all occurring simultaneously and influencing each other.

Not a static photo breathing, not slow-motion freeze-frame, no long poses. Movement is natural, fluid, and continuous, like a photographer capturing dynamic portraits while the subject moves freely.

Maintain character identity, face shape, and clothing stability; even with motion and temporary defocusing, it remains the same person upon refocusing.

title: Cinematic Urban Foot Chase Escape
description: A high-tension prompt for an urban foot chase where a teenager evades pursuers by vanishing around a corner.
promptText:
Boy = a 15-year-old teenage boy, slim and quick, short dark hair, wearing a hooded jacket, jeans, and sneakers, a backpack on his shoulders. Alert, scared, determined, athletic. Appearance only.

Chasers = three older guys in their 20s, casual streetwear, moving fast and aggressively as a group in pursuit. Appearance only.

City = a gritty urban environment — narrow streets, alleyways, brick walls, parked cars, market stalls, and a quiet side street around a corner. Overcast daytime light, realistic city textures. Environment only.

SCENE: a tense cinematic foot chase. A teenage boy with a backpack sprints through the city streets, chased by three older guys. He races through a busy street, then cuts hard around a corner into a quieter side street and quickly hides out of sight — and when the three chasers round the same corner moments later, the street is empty and they've lost him. A clever escape, no violence — pure suspense.

TECHNICAL: 16:9, cinematic handheld chase camera, dynamic tracking and running shots, urgent energy, slightly desaturated gritty urban grade, motion blur, shallow depth of field, photorealistic thriller quality.

CUTS:
CUT 1 (0-5s): The boy sprints down a busy street toward camera, backpack bouncing, glancing back in fear. Behind him, the three chasers give chase, weaving through pedestrians and market stalls. Handheld tracking shot conveying speed and panic.
CUT 2 (5-10s): The boy cuts hard around a street corner into a quieter side street. Fast tracking shot following him as he ducks behind a parked car / into a doorway / behind a wall, pressing himself out of sight, breathing hard, trying to stay silent.
CUT 3 (10-15s): The three chasers round the same corner at speed — and stop. The side street ahead is empty. They look around, confused, scanning the deserted street, having completely lost him. Hold on their frustration as the boy stays hidden. He's escaped.

RULES: References are appearance only, do not recreate. Keep the boy's appearance consistent across every cut. This is a suspenseful chase only — no weapons, no fighting, no physical contact, no violence. The tension comes from the pursuit and the clever escape. Sound design: pounding footsteps, heavy breathing, urban ambience, a tense driving score that drops to near-silence when he hides, then holds on the quiet as the chasers lose him. Final frame on the confused chasers and the empty street.
